start.text: The bramble wall stands higher than your head: canes as thick as a thumb, arched over and over each other, thorns as long as a finger. A few hips hang on it, red as coals.
The cart road's ruts run straight in under the canes. They do not come out on the other side, as far as you can see.
On a pine beside it, a cutter has cut the camp's notch for "this way home". It points into the thorns.
Your ember leans toward the brambles, very slightly, the way the Gull's cradle once leaned toward it.
